compatibility: Existing public configuration, plugin JSON-state contract, session/storage schema, event/exception fields and defaults are preserved.

Shared resume validates connector prerequisites before loading, then admits restoration, constructor and synchronous loaded notification in one transaction; rollback restores original bindings before candidate cleanup.
Partially constructed candidates release initialized framework resources. Errors preserve their original identity even when teardown throws.
JSON rollback snapshots honor own/prototype conversion hooks and Dates; serialization errors precede mutation.

Failed-plugin identity is process-local. Missing legacy keys keep existing restoration semantics but do not clear save protection. Successful trusted context.restoreState is an existing host repair path.
Tool registrations/namespace membership, execution pipeline authority, roles, prompt, callbacks, history and target rollback use existing host objects without cloning executables.
internalOnly: Per-plugin failed-rollback identities and successful-restoration tracking
supportBoundaries: Loads require idle execution/host mutation; separate contexts/backends need host concurrency coordination.
No rollback of external actions, model calls, arbitrary private hook/listener side effects or custom destructor resources.
Restore hooks must not await checkpoint IO on their own context.
Repair requires each affected instance actually restore successfully. Individual plugin method calls or omitted checkpoint keys are not proof. Rebuild context if its plugin cannot recover.
loadRaw retains its advanced unvalidated activation behavior; no authority is serialized.
Successful shared-context handoff still requires host ownership coordination.
